params.body:
#665 made the CI slower, not faster, and this puts that right.

**What the measurement said.** The runner of this job reports two usable cores, so `--parallel`
starts two test processes which then share those two cores with MariaDB. The `Run tests` step went
from 225s to 264s. On a development machine with six cores the same suite goes from 209s to 97s, so
the parallel machinery is worth having: `php artisan test --parallel` stays the local command, the
per-process database and the per-process storage stay, and the workflow now carries the number and
the condition under which the flag belongs there again (more cores).

**What does pay on both.** The most expensive thing in the suite is the demo seeder: 23 vehicles
times two photos, each encoded to three sizes plus the derived ones, about sixteen seconds a run.
Two tests ran it three times to ask two questions. They are one test now that runs it twice, and
the second run is exactly the repeat the idempotence test needed:

| | |
|---|---|
| `DemoScreensCommandTest` | 49s to 31s |

Nothing is pinned less: the same 96 assertions, the whole dataset and the repeat.

That is 18s off every run, everywhere. The step should land around 245s here, and the suite around
191s on a development machine serially, 80s in parallel.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: The CI runs the suite serially, and the demo seeder runs twice instead of three times
